subject: microbiology
title: Gram Staining, Acid-Fast Staining and the Peptidoglycan Cell Wall

steps.tx: **Gram staining** divides bacteria by cell wall architecture in four reagents: crystal violet primary stain, Gram iodine mordant, alcohol or acetone decolouriser (the decisive step), and safranin counterstain. Gram positive cells retain the crystal violet iodine complex in their thick peptidoglycan and read purple; gram negative cells lose it through a thin wall and outer membrane and read pink. Hans Christian Gram published the method in 1884 trying to see bacteria in lung tissue.
steps.say: Purple kept the dye, pink lost it; the decolouriser second decides every Gram stain.

vis.alt: Gram stain showing gram negative diplococci inside neutrophils
vis.caption: Gram stain of Neisseria gonorrhoeae, pink diplococci within neutrophils.

steps.tx: **Peptidoglycan** is the wall's load bearing mesh: alternating N acetylglucosamine and N acetylmuramic acid chains crosslinked by short peptides, thick and multilayered (20 to 80 nm, with teichoic acids) in gram positives, thin (2 to 7 nm) beneath an outer membrane in gram negatives. Lysozyme in tears cleaves its sugar backbone and penicillin blocks its peptide crosslinks, which is why wall anatomy predicts antibiotic behaviour.
steps.say: Thick mesh, no outer membrane: gram positive. Thin mesh plus outer membrane: gram negative.

left.title: Gram positive wall
points: No outer membrane, no periplasmic LPS

right.title: Gram negative wall
points: Outer membrane with LPS and porins

steps.tx: **Ziehl Neelsen staining** answers the wall Gram cannot read: mycobacteria wrap themselves in mycolic acid wax that refuses aqueous dyes, so carbol fuchsin is driven in with heat (or detergent in the cold Kinyoun method), acid alcohol cannot decolourise acid fast bacilli, and methylene blue counterstains the background. Auramine fluorescence screening is the same chemistry read by fluorescence microscopy at lower magnification.
steps.say: Mycolic wax refuses ordinary dye; hot carbol fuchsin enters and acid cannot evict it.

left.title: ZN steps
points: Acid alcohol decolouriser (3 percent HCl in ethanol)
Red bacilli on blue ground: acid fast positive

right.title: Acid fast cast
points: Mycobacterium tuberculosis and leprae (leprae weaker, Fite)

steps.tx: **Gram stain errors** are wall biology plus technique: old cultures and antibiotic damaged gram positives decolourise falsely gram negative (gram variable), thick smears under decolourise, mycobacteria stain weakly gram positive ghostly, and wall less organisms (Mycoplasma) and intracellular chlamydiae and rickettsiae do not Gram stain usefully at all. The report should name morphology and arrangement (cocci in chains, clusters, diplococci) because arrangement is diagnostic information.
steps.say: Report shape and arrangement, not only colour; old cultures lie about their Gram reaction.

left.title: Morphology vocabulary
points: Diplococci: pneumococcus lancet, Neisseria kidney shaped

right.title: Gram pitfalls
points: Old or damaged cells stain gram variable
Mycoplasma has no wall to stain

steps.tx: **Special stains complete** the morphology bench: Albert stain for Corynebacterium metachromatic (volutin) granules, India ink and nigrosin negative staining for capsules, Schaeffer Fulton for green endospores against red vegetative cells, silver impregnation (Fontana) for thin spirochaetes, and Giemsa for blood parasites and chlamydial inclusions. Each stain exists because one structure refuses the routine pair.
steps.say: Every special stain commemorates a structure the routine stains cannot show.

steps.tx: The gram negative **outer membrane** is a pharmacological border: porins admit small hydrophilic molecules (size and charge filtered), exclude vancomycin and many hydrophobics, and its lipopolysaccharide lipid A triggers Toll like receptor 4 into endotoxic shock physiology. Gram positive teichoic acids and peptidoglycan fragments inflame through TLR2 instead. Wall anatomy therefore predicts both drug entry and sepsis signalling.
steps.say: Porins decide drug entry, lipid A decides endotoxic signalling; the wall writes both.

nodes.label: Drug crosses gram negative outer membrane via porin
Shed LPS engages TLR4 on macrophages

steps.tx: **Gram stain remains** the fastest antibiotic compass in the laboratory: gram positive cocci in clusters in pus starts anti staphylococcal thinking, gram negative diplococci in urethral discharge or CSF redirects within the hour, long before culture identification. Its predictive value is highest in normally sterile fluids (CSF, joint, pleural) and weakest where colonising flora mixes, a specimen logic examinations test repeatedly.
steps.say: In sterile fluids the Gram stain prescribes the first antibiotic hour; in colonised sites it merely suggests.

left.title: High value Gram stains
points: CSF: diplococci versus bacilli redirect empiric therapy
Joint and pleural fluid in sepsis
Positive blood culture broth Gram stain

steps.tx: **Cell wall deficient** and wall unusual organisms close the topic: Mycoplasma and Ureaplasma (no peptidoglycan, sterols in membrane, beta lactam proof), mycobacteria (mycolic fortress), chlamydiae (developmental forms with minimal wall), and fungi (chitin and glucan, a different kingdom's wall). Beta lactam failure in atypical pneumonia is this paragraph arriving at the bedside on schedule.
steps.say: No peptidoglycan, no beta lactam effect; atypical pneumonia is wall anatomy presenting clinically.

left.title: Wall exceptions
points: Fungi: chitin and beta glucan wall

right.title: Clinical consequences
points: Beta lactams useless in mycoplasma pneumonia
Serology and NAAT replace Gram stain
